facts.text: Lidar sends short laser pulses and measures their return times to build a precise three-dimensional map of distances around a machine.
facts.quote: A lidar sends out very short laser pulses, times how long each takes to bounce back, and so builds a precise three-dimensional map of distances around the machine.

facts.text: Lidar simulation is the best validated of all sensor types.
facts.quote: Lidar simulation is the best validated of all sensor types.

facts.text: A ray-traced lidar model using the real scan pattern and full signal chain matched measurements with mean absolute percentage errors of 1.7% for amplitude, 8.5% for point count, and 9.3% for mean intensity, but only when the full processing chain and sensor imperfections were modeled.
facts.quote: matched measurements with a 1.7% mean absolute percentage error on amplitude and 8.5% and 9.3% on point count and mean intensity, but only when the full processing chain and the sensor's imperfections were modeled

facts.text: Adding rain and fog physics to the lidar model produced good agreement with weather-chamber data at low rain rates, but the mismatch grew in heavy rain.

facts.text: Fog is the best-reproduced condition in lidar simulation.

facts.text: Lidar could still measure range through dust with only 2% to 6% light transmission.

facts.text: Wet ground causes lost lidar returns and mirror points.
